title: Opening drift towards the map centre: early explore targets favour tiles nearer the middle
hypothesis: One behaviour, behind its own switch. In Targets::bestStaleTile (bot/targets.hpp), while w.round < P.openingRounds (new, start 60), add P.openingCentreWeight (new, start 2) x (torusDist(w.head, centre) - torusDist(t, centre)) to each grid tile's score, where centre = (W/2, H/2). Only explore targets change; pearl, spawn and farm targets don't. Why: maps are mirror or 180-degree symmetric, so (W/2, H/2) lies between our start and the enemy's mirrored start through the map's interior. Today every never-seen tile has the same staleness (staleCap), so 3*stale - 2*dist + 2*friendDist picks the nearest unseen grid tile just beyond vision, and dragons comb the ground next to home. Evidence (online submission 5300 vs team 63, 9 games): mean head distance from the centre at r0 -> r30, us vs them: Big Empty 37.0->40.1 vs 35.0->25.5, Schooltime 33.3->28.0 vs 32.3->18.0, Trauma 26.5->25.5 vs 25.5->20.3, stronghold 26.5->25.2 vs 25.5->21.5, Devil 15.0->10.7 vs 14.0->8.1, Default Small 11.0->9.0 vs 9.0->5.5, Default 26.0->20.8 vs 24.0->16.4, Trophy 18.0->11.8 vs 18.0->9.5, Queen of Spades 15.5->16.5 vs 15.5->15.2. Team 63 ends nearer the centre on 8 of 9 maps, covers more of the map (r60: Big Empty 64% vs our 35%) and ate more pearls by r100 on 7 of 9. Pearl spawn rate is not concentrated in the centre on most of these maps (rate-weighted distance to the centre is close to the all-tile mean except Trauma, stronghold, Devil and Trophy), so the claim is about reaching contested and unseen ground early, not about rich tiles. Example, Trauma 180466: team 63's dragon 1 walked west towards the middle and saw its gap-1 column at r7; our dragon 0 walked north along the map edge, passed 6 tiles west of our mirror column at r4-8 and wandered x 0-7 until r60; our team first saw our column at r20. Caveat: out-of-sight countdown targets pre-empt exploring on most turns (see the blind-target idea), so first log how many dragon-turns in r0-60 actually run chooseExplore. If under 20% on the ladder maps, report that instead of building. Scenarios: (1) r5 on an empty 64x64 map, a dragon at (13,14) with two unseen grid tiles equally far away, one towards (32,32) and one away: it picks the one towards the centre; (2) boundary: at round == P.openingRounds scores are unchanged; (3) a visible pearl or countdown target still wins over exploring; (4) a dragon already at the centre gets no pull. The region filter (scanRegion) only excludes tiles known to be unreachable (unseen edges count as open), so on walled maps the drift can aim across a wall we haven't seen yet; report how often the chosen tile's path is more than twice its straight-line distance. Report mean head distance to the centre at r10/20/30, team coverage at r60 and pearls r0-100 per map, against the champion and the gauntlet swarm.

title: A dragon with no pearl tile in view explores towards the map centre in the opening: on Devil we spend 68% of r1-30 in our empty home strip (leader 19%)
hypothesis: I132's direction, narrowed by a condition the bot can see, with Devil evidence. Devil is our worst map online (submission 6111: lost 11 of 21, 7 by elimination). Each side starts in a 6-column strip at its own edge (x 0-5, 26-31) with no pearl tiles; the pearl columns are towards the middle. Share of dragon-turns in r1-30 inside one's own home strip: us 0.68 (21 games), opponents 0.48, leader 55 0.19 (143305). Pearls per dragon-turn: 0.058 vs 0.084 vs 0.139. Pearls eaten in r0-30: 11.0 vs 16.9 vs 30. Mean head distance to the centre at r10/20/30: 13.1 vs 10.1 vs 5.8. Dragons / total length at r50: 10.5 / 28.4 vs 15.5 / 39.4 (leader 22 / 54). Watched: 234394 dragon 9 walked N up x=31 and S down x=30 for r1-22 with nothing in view and first ate at r23; dragons 7 and 11 did the same. Leader 55's six dragons walked W along the open band y 7-9 and were eating by r11. Big Empty shows a milder version: r0-30 eaten 23.6 vs 28.4, distance to centre 37.3 vs 32.5. It's our trait in wins too (home share 0.66 in Devil wins vs 0.70 in losses), so expect a gain in opening mass rather than a flipped result on its own. Cause: targets.hpp Targets::bestStaleTile. Every never-seen tile scores staleCap, so 3*stale - 2*dist + 2*friendDist picks the nearest unseen grid tile away from teammates, which is the empty strip at home. Change, behind its own switch: while w.round < P.openingRounds (new, start 60), and only when no visible tile has w.spawnKind == SPAWN_YES (the dragon sees nothing that can ever spawn a pearl), add P.openingCentreWeight (new, start 2) x (torusDist(head, centre) - torusDist(t, centre)) to each grid tile's score, with centre = (W/2, H/2). Pearl, spawn and farm targets are unchanged; only explore targets move. Scenarios: (1) Devil r3, a length-2 dragon at (31,8), nothing but empty tiles in view: its explore target is west of its head, towards x 16, not north or south along the strip. (2) The same dragon with one spawn tile in view: target unchanged from today. (3) Boundary: the same state at r60: unchanged. (4) A dragon with a pearl target: unchanged (explore isn't consulted). (5) A symmetric map whose home area has pearl tiles in view (Default Small): unchanged. Measure: home-strip share and pearls eaten in r0-30 on near_devil (baselines above), dragons and mass at r50, and wins on near_devil, near_big_empty, near_trophy. Check it costs nothing on stronghold and trauma, where the centre sits behind portals or kelp.

title: Re-check E0048's merge cascade beside the final fold: the champion with non-king merges switched off
hypothesis: Re-check of a behaviour accepted 9 promotions before this review, whose surroundings have changed. E0048 (+30) made any dragon die beside a visible teammate at least as long from P.mergeRound (then 300, now 450), within P.mergeRadius 2. Since then E0059 added the final fold over the sonar king beacon, and E0063 made folders merge only into the king (P.foldMergesOnlyKing) because each extra merge halves the mass again: in E0063's logging copy of the merge-into-any-longer-teammate version against the swarm, our longest ate 155 of the pearls our merges dropped and other dragons of ours 2250. The cascade still runs beside the fold for every dragon that is not folding (feed.hpp feedDirection, the branch returning P.mergeRadius from mergeRound). Online 6111 ends a game with total length 210 but longest 21.2 and second 15.3, while rank 1 ends with 130 and 27.2 and rank 2 with 72 and 29.4 (study.md, different opponents and maps, so a hint): we keep about 90% of our mass outside the tiebreak. Change, one new switch P.mergeCascade (true in the champion; this candidate sets it false): with it off, mateRadius returns -1 for every teammate but the reported king of an active fold, so a dragon merges only as a folder into the king within P.foldMergeRadius; seekFeeder, the fold, the king's protection and the end of ordinary splits at mergeRound stay as they are. Measure first with a logging copy against the champion, swarm and folder on about 12 maps (ladder, sprint, fresh eval), both sides: cascade merges a game after r450, the share of their dropped pearls the king eats against other dragons, longest and second at r499, with and without the switch. Expected: if cascade merges mostly move mass into non-kings that reach the king late or not at all, switching them off keeps more mass for folders that do reach it. Boundary: a dragon that hears no king report (the gap E0067 measured) loses its only way to consolidate, so the second-longest can fall and a team whose king dies late has less to fall back on; report both. Scenarios: at r460 a length-4 dragon two steps from a length-8 non-king teammate plays on with the switch off and dies beside it with it on; a folder within P.foldMergeRadius of the reported king merges either way; before mergeRound neither merges. If the SPRT ends H0 or even, the cascade stays.

title: A room the team has already seen is closed: the portal fallback asks the team's belief, not this dragon's own memory
hypothesis: Change (targets.hpp Targets::scanRegion, behind a new switch P.regionSeenByTeam): mark the region as still holding a never-seen tile only when seenForExplore(w, t) < 0 (the team's belief with P.beliefExplore), not w.lastSeen[t] < 0. bestStaleTile already ranks tiles by the team's staleness, so this matches the gate to the targets. Why: today a dragon keeps exploring its walkable region until it has personally seen every tile. But bestStaleTile rarely sends it to tiles a teammate saw lately, so the gate that lets it try an unknown portal stays shut for a long time, and a newborn child starts again from nothing. Evidence, online 6609, Trauma/Stronghold (264-tile start room sealed except for 1-2 portals): our first crossers are the oldest dragons, and late. 255126: dragon 1 (born r0) at r76, dragon 3 (r0) at r117. 254623: dragon 7 (born r1) at r101, 1 (r0) at r122, 3 (r0) at r159; children later (16, born r38, at r171). Stronghold: first crossing r120-r234 in the 9 games measured. Meanwhile we ate 5-7 pearls by r100 on Trauma to 566's 73-79, and 566 was at its farm from r19. The leader (162466, same side of Trauma) crossed at r12, r26 and r57. Only closed regions are affected: a region that reaches never-seen ground (most open maps; Schooltime's 77% region) keeps today's behaviour. Independent of the walled-pearl trigger: this one fires in a sealed room even when nothing behind the wall is in view. Scenarios: (1) Trauma side-B start room fully reported by 4 teammates by ~r25: a child born at r30 with no pearl target heads for the nearest unknown portal instead of touring the room; (2) the region still has a tile no teammate has reported: unchanged; (3) no unknown portal in the region: unchanged; (4) boundary: P.beliefExplore off gives the old behaviour; portal-free maps play identical games. title: A small team keeps out of every enemy head's reach: while we have fewer than P.smallTeamUnits dragons, an equal or longer head is a bad rammer too
hypothesis: Defensive mirror of I125 (our own unit count gates our even rams). 6824 (v0028, unswbc-1.1.0) lost 6 of 10 unranked games to the dev benchmark; 3 were eliminations by r140-164 on the three smallest ladder maps (Trophy 263246, Devil 263247, Default Small 263560), with 8, 4 and 4 dragons at r100 against 27, 39 and 18. In r0-150 nearly every death of ours there was a head-on (30 of 30, 24 of 32, 20 of 22), and the dev started 16, 12 and 4 of them, mostly 3-on-2, 2-on-2 and 3-on-3. Safety::badRammer marks an enemy head as a bad trade for us only when it is shorter than us (tradeGood), or equal-or-longer while headEdge <= P.ramGuardMaxEdge (-1, E0060's guard), so in a 1-on-1 window an equal or longer head is fine to stand beside, which holds only while losing a dragon costs little. Change, behind P.smallTeamUnits (start 12; 0 turns it off): while World::unitCount < P.smallTeamUnits, badRammer is true for every visible enemy head, so riskyFor charges P.riskPenalty on its one-step reach (escape.hpp's bad-rammer set follows); trades we start are I125's subject and stay as they are here. Scenarios: a team of 5, our length-3 head beside a pearl that an equal enemy head can also step onto next turn, with another safe move: we take the safe move; the same with 20 dragons: we take the pearl as today; a team of 5 where every move is in reach: the least-bad move is still played (the penalty only orders moves). Measure first with a logging copy vs breeder and swarm on small maps (near_default_small, near_devil, near_trophy, gen tiny and normal): head-ons suffered per game while small, our dragons at r100, eliminations; if our r100 count does not rise, report that.

title: Drop a pearl target for a while once the move scoring refuses to step onto it
hypothesis: Change: when the pearl target (Targets::pearl) is one step from our head and evaluateMove refused that step for a pocket (it took the closed-pocket or room-shortfall penalty, shortfallPerTile, because farmEntryOk didn't accept the pocket), remember the tile. choosePearl skips it for P.refusedTargetRounds rounds (new, default 20), so the dragon picks the next pearl or explores. Only pocket refusals count, not riskyFor or teammate-exit penalties, which change from turn to turn. Why: choosePearl ranks pearls by path length and never asks whether evaluateMove will let us in, so a lone pearl in a dead end stays the target and the dragon circles beside it. Evidence: Schooltime (1,11) and its mirror (58,11) sit in a 1-tile pocket (kelp W and S, a portal on the E edge, one open side). To a dragon that hasn't crossed that portal it is a dead end, and farmEntryOk needs 2+ pearls. 263245 dragon 14 looped the 2x2 beside it for about 36 rounds (r100-136). The pearl sat there 413 of 500 rounds and we never ate it; 545 ate its own mirror pocket's pearl 5 times. 151 of our 234 flagged Schooltime pearl moves (blunders.py) are next to this pocket. Same mechanism with a teammate's body at a pocket's mouth: 263245 r356-372, dragon 385 circled for 16 rounds beside (47,11) (earlier audit F6, Trauma (24,8)). Stuck runs (8+ rounds within 3 steps of the same uneaten pearl, not eating): Schooltime 543, 380, 389 and 229 dragon-rounds a game for us v 215, 304, 128 and 104 for the opponent; Trauma vs 15 and 106 379 and 306 v 0. That is 2-3% of our dragon-time there. Tests: (1) a length-2 dragon beside a 1-tile pocket pearl whose only other side is an unknown portal: it stops targeting it the turn after the refusal and walks to another pearl or explores; (2) a pocket with a teammate at its mouth: same; (3) boundary: a pocket holding 2+ pearls that farmEntryOk accepts is still entered and farmed; (4) a pearl refused only because an enemy head could ram us there stays a target; (5) after P.refusedTargetRounds the tile can be chosen again, e.g. once a teammate has crossed and paired the portal.

title: A small team avoids even trades, not just declines them: while unitCount < P.evenTradeMinUnits, a tile an enemy head at least as long can step onto next is risky
hypothesis: E0107 (I125) stopped our dragons starting rams on enemy heads no longer than themselves while we have fewer than P.evenTradeMinUnits (12) dragons, and lost (SPRT H0, -13.7 Elo; vs champion 0.43, swarm 0.51, rammer 0.50, breeder 0.49). The trades still happened, with the opponent starting them: in the 40 kept losses, while we had under 12 dragons we suffered 427 even-or-up head-ons started by the enemy (champion 113, breeder 84, swarm 99, rammer 30) against 112 started by us (mostly doomed one-step moves and sprints). Watched: 0392 r24 our lower-id length-2 dragon 0 declined the equal head 2 away, stepped onto a pearl beside it, and the enemy sprint-rammed it (WS); 0086 r10 our length-3 dragon with 2 allies in view (edge +1) declined, moved N, and the enemy moved first next round and sprint-rammed it; 0017 r51 the same with a 3-step sprint. Declining gives the opponent the choice of when to trade, and it trades where its side is at least tied locally, so its side eats the drop. Build on the candidate: Safety::badRammer also returns true for d.visibleLen >= w->length when w->unitCount < P.evenTradeMinUnits (behind its own switch P.smallTeamRamGuard), exactly as P.outnumberedRamGuard does when outnumbered in view, so riskyFor makes our small team keep one step out of an equal head's reach instead of walking beside it. The escape sprint (escape.hpp) and hunt read badRammer too; say how often each fires with the new switch. Scenarios: a length-3 dragon of an 8-dragon team with a pearl north beside an equal enemy head takes another open move; at P.evenTradeMinUnits dragons it eats the pearl as today; surrounded by equal heads it still steps onto an empty tile (not doomed); a shorter enemy head beside the pearl is ignored. title: Guard the future king before the fold: only the locally longest dragon (12+) avoids a shorter head's sprint reach, from r100
hypothesis: Endgame arithmetic (review 1790404915361643000). A dead dragon's pearls lie on every second body tile, all one checkerboard colour (docs/unsw/execution-order.md, death sequence), and a single step changes colour, so a king eats a corpse's drop at most every other move: from P.foldRound (397) the fold can add about 0.5 x 103 = 51. In this review's 6 kept rule-count games of champion 2c79f81 our longest grew +40, +38, +16, +38, +40 over r400-499, and the breeder (never folds) grew its longest +46 and +38 by eating alone, so round 500 is decided by our longest when the fold starts. Ours at r400 was 57, 5, 15, 12 and 5; rank 1's on Big Empty (study replay 162468) grew steadily at the 64 cap, 9 at r80 to 27 at r400, then 56 at r499 without folding. Ours stays short because it dies: dragons 12+ long that were our team's longest died 30 times before r397 in those 6 games (about 5 a game), 15 of them head-on to enemy heads 2-6 long, the rest trapped (I257's case). Every sprint-reach guard so far covered all long dragons, so its pearl cost fell on many dragons that don't decide the tiebreak (E0075, length >= 5: -5.0, 83% of firings before r410, 55% on length 5-9; E0098, length >= 10: -3.6, open near_big_empty 0.57 against corridor maps ~0.40); I166 (in flight) covers 10+ only from the beacon round. Change, behind a new switch, on I166's markSprintReach code (cherry-pick its candidate if it isn't kept): from P.kingGuardFromRound (start 100), a dragon at least P.kingGuardMinLength (start 12) long with no longer teammate in view and no fresh king report of a longer one treats tiles a strictly shorter bad rammer can reach by a 2-3 step sprint this turn as risky, while some unmarked steady move exists; every other dragon plays as the champion. Scenarios (lengths through P): a 20-long dragon at r200 with a length-4 head 2 steps away takes an unmarked move instead of the pearl between them; boundary: the same dragon with a 25-long teammate in view takes the pearl; an 11-long dragon takes it; every steady move marked: the champion's move. Measure first with a logging copy vs champion, swarm and breeder: guarded dragon-turns a game (expect 1-3 dragons at a time), their pearls eaten, deaths of our team's longest 12+ before r397 by cause, and our longest at r397 and r499; if guarded turns don't cut head-on deaths of the longest, stop with the numbers.

By map family, eligible maps only: near_devil 0.587 (n=23), near_snake_trap 0.575 (20), near_trophy 0.523 (22), near_great_divide 0.524 (21), gen-normal 0.468 (100, the largest group), near_dilemma 0.420 (22), near_default 0.348 (23), near_queen_of_spades 0.272 (23). In the replays the centre was simply empty on generated maps and on Default: on near_default the teams meet across the wrap edge and the centre (15,15) is the back of both. On Queen of Spades both of our dragons walked to an empty centre while the opponent's ate a patch near the wrap corner by r38. So a centre bias only pays where the map was built with a pile there, and a dragon can't see that before arriving. I191 changes only blind explore targets, not pearl or countdown targets, so it should cost less than E0114 did. Test it with an explicit check that the gen-normal and near_default families are not worse, and drop it if they are. title: A pearl target whose last step the move scorer refuses is replaced, so dragons stop hovering beside pearls they won't take (410 of 464 such turns at the unit cap)
hypothesis: Audit of bot/targets.hpp (this review). Targets::choosePearl ranks pearls by path cost and never asks whether evaluateMove will take the final step, so when the scorer refuses the step onto an adjacent target (a closed pocket farmEntryOk rejects, E0106's cut-off penalty P.headReachPenalty near the cap, a teammate's only exit, an enemy's ram reach) the target stays and every other move is ordered by distance to that refused pearl: the dragon hovers beside it. Measured from the 6 kept replays of this review's rule-count games (champion 5f37cbf, debug line target + board frames, scratch script): 464 logged turns had a visible target pearl one path step away, not taken, while the chosen move carried no survival penalty (score above -1e5); 410 of them with 62+ of our dragons alive, 435 in one 64x64 game against the breeder; an enemy head was beside the pearl in only 6 and a teammate head in 57. Over all pearl-target runs, 3,208 ended with the dragon on the tile, 2,705 switched away from a pearl still there and 3,959 ended with the tile empty. I259 (the Schooltime (1,11) pocket: 263245 dragon 14 looped beside it about 36 rounds) is the pocket case of the same defect and is merged here. Change, behind P.dropRefusedTarget: after evaluateMoves, when the pearl target is one step away and that step is not MoveEval::safe while another move is safe, run choosePearl again with that tile excluded and re-evaluate the moves once; optionally remember the tile for P.refusedTargetRounds (start 0 = this turn only; I259 proposed 20 for pocket refusals only, and the coder picks with a measurement). Complement of E0106 (kept on probability, +4.0): its guard refuses moves that the target still points at. Scenarios: (1) at 63 dragons a 6-long dragon whose step onto the adjacent target is cut off, with a second pearl 5 open steps away, heads for the second; (2) boundary: the same position 3 dragons below the cap margin eats the first; (3) a lone pocket pearl farmEntryOk rejects, nothing else in reach: it explores instead of circling; (4) a pocket farmEntryOk accepts is still entered and farmed. CPU: the extra choosePearl and evaluateMoves run on about 2% of turns; check p99. Report hovering (8+ rounds within 3 steps of the same uneaten target) and pearls eaten a game, at and below the cap.
history: 2026-09-27 02:26 orchestrator: E0136's post-mortem watched one more instance (diagnostic game 0004, near_trauma): a length-2 dragon circled 4 tiles for 60 rounds beside a pearl in a 2x2 pocket full of pearl-spawn tiles. Its coder also suspects the closed-pocket rule (Safety::floodFill, reachedFreed) is wrong for a dragon of length 3 or less, which can turn round in a 2x2 pocket. title: Long dragons graze where the enemy isn't: pearl and explore targets for our 12+ dragons cost extra in blocks where the team recently saw an enemy head
hypothesis:
New (related to I062, which is for short dragons, and I273/I280, which are local sprint-reach guards).

The unused evidence:
- The team already builds and gossips per-block enemy sightings: belief.hpp `enemyRound`/`enemyThere`, sent as `rec.enemy`.
- `Belief::enemyChance(b, now)` (belief.hpp:380) turns them into a fading probability, but nothing that decides a move or target calls it.

Evidence (audit 1790429282522188000, F2):
- In all 4 v0032 Big Empty losses we trailed at r400 and grew as fast as the opponent afterwards; the gap came earlier.
- Our longest (12+) was killed by 3-6 long rammers 6-8 times before r400 in 296354/296056/295719, against 0-1 for the opponent.
- Share of r150-396 rounds where our longest had an enemy head in view: 0.35 and 0.39, against 306's 0.07 and 27's 0.08. Those two beat us by 20 and 17.
- Across 10 Big Empty games (ours plus the leaders'), the less exposed longest won 7; the earlier audit found 10 of 11 over r300-499.
- 306's king had no enemy head in view for 88 straight rounds (r240-327) while it grew from 21 to 33.

Change, behind a switch, modelled on Targets::crowdAt: for a dragon at least P.guardMinLength (start 12) long, add weight x max(0, enemyChance - P.enemyPrior) summed over the target's block and its 8 neighbours to each pearl and explore target's cost. Start around 6 steps per unit of chance. With no reports (the uniform prior) it adds nothing, so choices change only where an enemy head was actually seen.

Scenarios to test:
- A 20-long dragon with two equal pearls, one in a block where a teammate reported an enemy head 2 rounds ago: it picks the other.
- The same with the report 40 rounds old: evidence faded, no change.
- A 6-long dragon: unchanged.
- Boundary: exactly 12 long.

Score it against the `hunter` screen entry as well as the rotation, since rotation opponents rarely stalk long dragons.

title: Measure first: does the reversing split (I130) pay against opponents that stalk long dragons?
hypothesis:

title: Leave a sealed start room once the team has seen it: the portal fallback reads team belief, only when our closed region is at most 30% of the map
hypothesis: Builds on I229, with a size gate so that E0054's shortcut-portal loss can't return. PROBLEM: on Trauma and Stronghold the start room is sealed by kelp. It is 264 tiles (22% of the map) and its only exits are 1-2 portal pairs (map files). On every other ladder map the portal-free start region is 75-100% of the map (Portals 40%). EVIDENCE (v0032 online): our first dragon leaves the Trauma room at r56-94 in 5 of 11 games and after r100 in 6; opponents leave at r10-53 in 9 of 11. On Stronghold we never leave before r100 in 6 of 6; opponents leave at r10-37 in 4. Where either side left before r100, the opponent left first in 13 of 15 (sign p = 0.004). In every decisive game of those we ate fewer pearls in r0-99: 12 of 12 (p = 0.0002; ours 3-67, theirs 13-152). Record on the two maps 9-8, against 94-34 elsewhere (suggestive). CAUSE: the team had seen every room tile by r20-53 in 16 of 17 games, yet the first exit came 30-110 rounds later. Targets::scanRegion (targets.hpp:314) asks the dragon's own w.lastSeen whether a never-seen tile is left, so every split child (born with no memory) must see all 264 tiles itself before chooseExplore's portal fallback can fire; E0125's mirroring leaves lastSeen untouched. CHANGE (behind a switch): when the region scanRegion walks over known edges has an unknown portal on its edge and holds at most P.sealedRoomShare (0.3) of W*H tiles, count a tile as seen if the team's belief has seen it (seenForExplore), not only our own memory. Everything else stays as today: the fallback still needs no pearl target (pearl < 0) and still targets the nearest unknown portal. OUT OF SCOPE, as a follow-up once this is measured: Stronghold's room holds 99 spawn tiles, so spawn targets may still keep dragons there. MEASURE with a logging copy: first unknown-portal crossing round and r0-99 pearls on Trauma and Stronghold, both sides; expect crossings by about r30-50 instead of r60-130. Games on every other ladder map must be identical, since their regions are over 30% of the map. SCENARIOS: (1) Trauma-like room (11x24 in a 48x24 map, kelp all round, 2 unknown portals), team belief has seen every tile, a fresh child that has seen only its 7x7 targets the nearest portal and crosses; (2) the same room with one tile no teammate has seen, no change; (3) boundary: a closed region of exactly 30% of the map fires, one tile more does not; (4) an open map with portals (region 90%) where the team has seen everything plays exactly as today; (5) a pearl target in the room still wins over the portal, as today. SPRT on a mix that includes the official trauma~k and stronghold~k variants plus the usual fresh maps; most pairs will be identical.

title: Hunt a lone enemy king from shared sightings in the fold (same change as I052)
hypothesis: Same change as I052 (hunt from shared sightings), with new evidence that makes the fold its first case. PROBLEM: some opponents fold all-in and leave their king almost alone. In 7 of our 27 round-limit losses (26%, 95% range 13-45%) there were rounds from r400 where the opponent had at most 5 dragons, we had at least twice as many, and their longest beat ours: 300725 v 20 for 77 rounds, 299219 v the dev 66, 298370 v 762 60, 296885 v 740 58, 295871 v 91 22, 300723 v 20 17, 302120 v 218 11. Killing that king would have won 5 of the 7: their next-longest was 5, 17, 16, 23 and 14, against our longest of 14, 24, 25, 33 and 15. WATCHED: 300725 r424-499, team 20 is down to 2-5 dragons with a 15-23-long king, and several of our 3-9-long dragons are 5-13 steps away the whole time; none comes within 3 steps, so findRam never fires. 299219 r440-499: the dev has 3 dragons and a 22-28-long king, and our 2-3-long dragons are 5-10 steps away. CAUSE: huntDirection (hunt.hpp) only chases heads in the 7x7 view, within huntMaxDist 6, and only with dragons at most hunterMaxLength 5 long; from foldRound short dragons walk to our own king instead. CHANGE (behind a switch): from P.foldRound, a dragon that is not our king and at most P.loneKingHunterMax long walks toward the last shared sighting of an enemy head at least as long as our king's report, when it holds such a report no older than a few rounds and within P.loneKingReach path steps. It does so instead of folding while the enemy heads the team has seen since foldRound are few (at most P.loneKingMaxEnemies, e.g. 5). Enemy lengths over sonar are I090's record; build that first, or send the sighting's length with the enemy block evidence. SCENARIOS: (1) r430, one 20-long enemy head reported 9 steps from our 4-long dragon, 3 enemy heads seen since foldRound: the dragon walks toward it and rams it once findRam reaches it; (2) the same with 12 enemy heads seen: it folds as today; (3) our king itself never hunts; (4) boundary: a report one round older than the age limit is ignored; (5) before foldRound nothing changes. MEASURE the trigger first with a logging copy against the earlyfold/folder/grower screen entries (the opponents that fold all-in): rounds a game in the state above, and how often a hunter reaches ram range.

title: Measure first: head-ons we start while a swarm outnumbers us 3:1, then refuse them all (equal and longer victims)
hypothesis: Related to I290/I291, which only cover equal-length rams; a third of the rams here were on longer heads. EVIDENCE (v0032 online): in three eliminations (302039 Trophy and 302040 Devil v 370, 300722 Autarky v team 20) we started 58 head-ons while the whole enemy team outnumbered ours 3:1 or worse, and 41 at 2-3:1, against 12 below 2:1. At 3:1 or worse we started 58 and suffered 40 (p = 0.04). Of the 58: 31 on equal heads, 25 on longer heads, 6 on shorter. In 302040, with 3 dragons against 35-46, ours still moved into enemy heads at r265, r269 and r289. 370's longest was 3-4 all game, so any 5-long dragon alive at r500 beats it on the tiebreak. It eliminated us on Devil, Trophy and Prisoners Dilemma and lost to us at r500 or by elimination on Schooltime and Autarky. CAUSE: P.minUnitsToTrade (3) looks only at our own count; Safety::attackGood judges length, not units; E0115's met-id guard declined only equal rams and left our dragon in reach (flat). SCENARIOS: (1) 3 of ours against 30 met ids: a 2-long beside a 4-long enemy head steps away instead of ramming; (2) 10 of ours against 20 met ids (2:1): rams as today; (3) a met enemy 8 long: rams as today (a grower is not a swarm); (4) boundary: ratio exactly 3.0 fires, 2.9 does not; (5) when the only non-fatal move is the ram, it still rams.

title: Opening portal scouts: a starting dragon that knows an unknown portal near it crosses it before farming, as the teams that take Schooltime's garden do
hypothesis: Change (behind P.openingScouts). Who scouts: a dragon born at round 0 (a starter; Default's round-0 split children count), before round P.scoutUntil (start 60), and until it has crossed P.scoutCrossings (start 2) unknown portals. What it does: while scanRegion finds a tile beside an unknown portal within P.scoutPortalReach (start 20) BFS steps, (a) Targets::update keeps only pearl targets within P.scoutGrab (start 2) steps, and (b) chooseExplore takes that portal tile as the explore target with explorePortalDir set, instead of only when the region has no never-seen tile. evaluateMove then crosses it: crossesExplorePortal needs pearl < 0, which (a) gives. Split children and every dragon after P.scoutUntil play as today. A map with no unknown portal near a starter plays identical games. Why: our dragons don't cross portals in the opening, and the ground behind them decides several ladder maps (audit findings F2-F3). Schooltime's 26-tile fast garden (x27-32, y34-38) can't be reached on foot: walking covers 77% of the map, with portals the garden is 33 steps (maps/ladder/schooltime.map matches the server's). In 27 Schooltime games of 7359/7577 our heads never stand on it before r200. We reach it in 6 games, at r382-487. Opponents stand on it in 12 games and eat 182-459 fast pearls from it: the dev 427 and 451, 552 459, 370 406. We lost 5 of those 12 and 1 of the other 15 (Fisher p = 0.043). In the 4 games traced, the first entrant was a starter or its first child. It crossed a portal beside its start at r10-12 ((38,10)->(13,18) or (57,11)->(1,21)), then (11,25)->(28,25) at r21-37, and reached the garden at r34-50; its children farmed it (the dev had 81-117 dragon-rounds a 20-round window on fast tiles in r40-119 of 305931). Our first portal crossing on Schooltime is r44-180 (none by r200 in 3 of 27), with 0-1 crossings in r0-99. Across Schooltime, Trophy and Default, all 16 of our losses in 72 games were to opponents that crossed a portal by r61: 16 of 30 such games lost, 0 of 42 against later or no crossers (p = 3.5e-8, confounded with opponent strength). On Trauma, 8 of 8 losses were to opponents crossing by r27, and none of 7 against later or none; we cross at r56-133. The code: chooseExplore runs only when choosePearl found nothing (targets.hpp:81). A portal becomes the target only when scanRegion finds no never-seen tile, judged on the dragon's own lastSeen (targets.hpp:281-316), and crossing needs pearl < 0. So E0054, E0062 and E0064's portal frontiers sat behind the pearl-target block; E0054's logging copy first crossed on Schooltime at r144. E0054 lost where portals lead into known ground; before r60 almost nothing is known, and only starters scout. Measure first (logging copy, P.scoutUntil 60), with a stop condition. On Schooltime, both sides, 4 seeds: the scout or its descendants stand on the garden by r70 in at least 3 of 4 games. Our fast pearls in r0-199 go from 0 to over 100. Trauma's first crossing moves below r30. If not, stop and report where the scouts went. Scenarios: (1) a starter 6 steps from an unknown portal, with a visible pearl 4 steps the other way, walks to the portal and crosses. (2) The same with the pearl 2 steps away eats it first. (3) A split child in the same place farms as today. (4) A starter after r60 farms as today. (5) After 2 crossings the scout farms. (6) A portal whose far end is known (paired) is an ordinary path, not a scout target. (7) Boundary: Devil and Big Empty (no portals) play identical games. Slithery Fight has 7 packed starters at pump slots: report its r0-99 intake against the champion (545-576 today), since leaving pumps there is the risk. Queen of Spades and Portals (portals into small pockets, 3-6% of the map) should cost at most the scouts' r0-60 pearls.

title: Same change as I191: in the opening, a dragon with no pearl tile in view explores towards the map centre (new Devil evidence: the centre by r25 decides every game)
hypothesis: Same change as I191, with new evidence from 18 Devil games of 7359/7577. The side that ate more fast pearls in r0-99 won all 17 games measured: we won 10 of 10 where we ate more and lost 7 of 7 where they did (one-sided Fisher p = 5e-5). In losses we ate 17-53 against 91-131; in wins 98-141 against 1-48. The centre block (14,7), (17,7), (14,8), (17,8) and the gap-30 column x15-16 sit in x12-19. The home strips x0-4 and x27-31 hold no pearl tile, so I191's gate holds there. Before contact (r5-29), the opponent had fewer dragon-rounds within 6 steps of its start than we did in 6 of 7 losses: ours 0.59-0.77, theirs 0.22-0.53. That was true in only 1 of 11 wins (p = 0.0025). Our own share barely moves; the rushers (218, 370, 46, the dev) decide it. Heads in the centre box, us/them: 294949 v dev r20 1/4, r30 2/6, r40 0/12. Watched 305933: the dev's three starters walk straight west to x18-22 by r12. Our dragon 10 spends all of r1-35 in x0-4, and dragon 6 r1-17, sweeping the strip. Against the dev we are 1-9 on Devil across all builds, all 9 losses eliminations. The cause: Targets::bestStaleTile (targets.hpp:351) scores 3*stale - 2*torusDist + 2*friendDist, with every never-seen tile at staleCap 60. So in the opening the nearest never-seen tile always wins, and the target is dropped once visible, even across kelp. The bot knows W and H; the map centre lies on the mirror line for all three guaranteed symmetries, and on Devil and Trophy the fast ground is there. Scenarios: (1) Devil starters at x0-3 reach x12-19 by r15; count heads in x12-19 at r20 and r25 against the champion. (2) On Trophy the centre is inside the cup: the target must be walkable, and it is through the cup's open bottom (y15-16). (3) A dragon with a pearl tile in view is unchanged. (4) Boundary: Slithery Fight, Autarky and Prisoners Dilemma, where home holds pearl tiles and we win now, should play nearly identically; report their r0-99 intake. (5) Big Empty (no centre resource) should not lose r0-99 intake.

title: Same change as I294: race for the centre on small maps (Trophy: we eat no centre fast pearls in 7 of 7 losses)
hypothesis: Same change as I294, with new Trophy evidence from 21 games of 7359/7577. The fast tiles (gap 5-30) sit in the cup's middle, x10-14, y7-10. We ate at most 1 of them in r0-99 in 7 of 7 losses (the opponent 26-43), and in 3 of 13 wins (Fisher p = 0.0015). Every loss was to an opponent whose first portal crossing came by r61. We went 11-0 against the rest (p = 0.001). The cup is 19 steps from a start on foot, through its open bottom; the portal pair (12,22)/(12,23) <-> (12,5)/(12,6) beside the lower start makes it 11. How opponents got in: 305932, dev dragon 3 walked (20,22) -> (12,22), crossed at r26 and stood on the fast tiles at r30. 304251 (306) crossed at r15 and was in at r19. 294948 (dev 3) walked up (15,22) -> (15,12) by r15. Ours in 305932: dragon 0 stays in rows y1-3 (x4-10) until it dies by r28; the lower starter 2 goes (4,22) -> (10,24) -> (10,2) and dies by r20. Against the dev we are 2-9 on Trophy, all 9 losses eliminations. The cause is the nearest-first explore of F1 (targets.hpp:351), and on Trophy the carpet of slow pearl tiles means choosePearl nearly always has a target, so chooseExplore (targets.hpp:81) rarely runs. Scenarios: (1) on Trophy, our heads in the cup (x7-17, y4-15) at r20 and r30, and fast pearls in r0-99, against the champion. (2) The lower starter reaches the cup through the open bottom, or the portal once it is paired. (3) Boundary: Default (no centre resource, 19% of the map behind portals) should not lose r0-99 intake; Big Empty should play the same or better.

title: Same change as I335: leave a sealed start room once the team has seen it (Trauma: 8 of 8 losses to opponents who left by r27; the 30% gate misses Schooltime's garden pocket)
hypothesis: Same change as I335, with new evidence. On Trauma, all 8 losses in 15 games of 7359/7577 were to opponents whose first portal crossing came by r27 (r10-27). We lost none of 7 against opponents crossing at r33-53 or not at all (Fisher p = 0.0002). Our own first crossing is r56-133. 305934 (7577 v dev): our dragon-rounds within 6 of our start in r25-124 were 0.79 against the dev's 0.30; pearls r0-99 7 v 22; first crossing r119 against r13. 306287 (7577 v 733, lost): r92 against r17. The cause is unchanged in v0036: Targets::scanRegion decides 'the region still holds a never-seen tile' from the dragon's own w.lastSeen (targets.hpp:316), not from team belief, and split children are born with no memory. Walkable start region per map, from the map files: Trauma 23%, Portals 41%, Default 81%, Schooltime 77%. So I335's 30% gate is right for Trauma, and it leaves Schooltime's portal-only garden pocket to the scout idea from this audit. Scenarios: (1) on Trauma, our first crossing and pearls in r0-99 against the champion. (2) Boundary: Default and Schooltime (region above 30%) play identical games. (3) Portals (41%) plays identical games unless the gate is raised; report it separately if it is.

title: Same change as I252: a small team keeps out of equal and longer enemy heads' reach (the dev finishes us by ramming, not by our rams)
hypothesis: Same change as I252, with new evidence from the three eliminations by the dev in this batch: 305929 Default, 305932 Trophy and 305933 Devil. While we were outnumbered 3:1 or worse we lost 87 dragons. 48 were enemy heads moving into ours, 45 of them by an enemy head as long as ours or longer. 29 were our heads moving into theirs. 10 were walls, bodies or self (the dev moved in on 48 of 77 head-ons, sign test p = 0.02). So declining our own rams (I338) would address only a third of the dying. The dev's longest at the end was only 10, 7 and 5. Our longest never passed 4 while outnumbered, so surviving alone doesn't win the tiebreak; this caps losses rather than winning games. Priority 3 because the opening (the Devil and Trophy ideas from this audit) decides these games first. Scenarios: (1) with 5 dragons against 15, a 3-long of ours with an equal enemy head 2 steps away steps out of its one-step reach when a safe step exists. (2) With 20 dragons, unchanged. (3) Report, on Devil and Trophy against the swarm and rammer entries, the deaths per game by 'they moved into us' against the champion.

title: Opening plan by map shape: starters read whether their home region is sealed (only portals or a few doors lead out) or open, and play I355's portal scouts, I191's centre drift or today's opening accordingly
hypothesis:
Big picture, conditional not constant (sig 2026-09-25): one opening pulls opposite ways by map shape. E0114 (centre rush, -5.3) read near_big_empty 0.62 (23 trials, z +2.8) but near_default 0.35 and near_queen_of_spades 0.27 (z -3.5, -5.3). The briefing's 13-map study: our five worst ladder maps (Devil, Stronghold, Trauma, Portals, Slithery Fight; 44-43 against 196-74 elsewhere, per-map win 0.47 v 0.62, p = 0.001 of 23 features) are walled boards cut into halves joined by 1-5 passable edges or only by portals, fast pearls in 1-wide corridors and dead ends. On Schooltime, Trophy and Default all 16 of our losses in 72 games were to opponents that crossed a portal by r61 (audit, confounded with strength); on Devil the side that ate more fast pearls in r0-99 won all 17 games. I191 (drift to the centre when nothing in view can spawn) and I355 (starters cross a near unknown portal first) each fit one shape.

Build after both are tested, stacked on their candidates if they left ones: a named situation read by r20 from scanRegion's region, with E0125's mirrored edges: sealed (the region's border to unseen ground is only unknown portals, or at most P.doorMax (start 3) passable edges, once the home region holds no never-seen tile) or open. Sealed: I355's scouts; open with no spawn tile in view: I191's drift; otherwise today's opening. Each branch keeps the switch of the idea it borrows; the situation is logged in the debug line.

Scenarios: Portals (halves joined only by portals): starters scout; Big Empty (open, pearls everywhere): today's; Devil (empty home strip, centre on foot): drift. Boundary: unclassified by r20: today's.

Fire rate: measure first, from the map files and a logging copy: the classification's accuracy on the 13 organiser maps and 20 generated ones, and branch counts a game. If I191 and I355 both read flat or worse, there is nothing to switch between: drop with that. Map mix near 0.5. Default bounds.
